candidates.statement: Thus the quantity $R(a_j,a_j)$ appearing in (\ref{dlog_tau}) must be interpreted to mean \[ \lim_{y\rightarrow a_j \atop y\in J} R(a_j,y); \] similarly for $p_j$ and $q_j$ in (\ref{qp_defn}) and like quantities appearing later.

The definitions of $u$ and $v$ must be modified to read \begin{equation} u=\left(A\chiJ,\left(I-K\right)^{-1}A\right),\ \ \ v=\left(A\chiJ,\left(I-K\right)^{-1}A^\prime\right)\, . \label{uv_defn2} \end{equation} Notice that since \[ \left(I-K\right)^{-1} A = \left(I-K\right)^{-1} A \chiJ \ \ \ {\rm in }\ J \] this agrees with the original definitions of $u$ and $v$ given by (\ref{uv_defn}). \par We can think of $K$ as an operator taking smooth functions to smooth functions and so the operators $KD$ and $DK$ make sense, the former having distributional kernel.

First, we have the easy fact \[ {\partial\over\partial a_k} K\doteq (-1)^k K(x,a_k)\delta(y-a_k) \] and so by (\ref{dResolvent_dalpha}) \begin{equation} {\partial\over \partial a_k} \left(I-K\right)^{-1} \doteq (-1)^k R(x,a_k) \rho(y-a_k) \, . \label{dR2} \end{equation} At this point we must keep in mind that $Q$ and $P$ are functions of $a$ as well, and so we denote them now by $Q(x,a)$ and $P(x,a)$, respectively.

Since, clearly, both sides tend to zero as all $a_i\rightarrow\infty$, their difference must be identically zero. \par To deduce (\ref{uv_2}) we add (\ref{CR_5}) and (\ref{dR2}) to obtain \[ \left( {\partial\over\partial x}+{\partial\over\partial y}+ \sum_k {\partial\over\partial a_k}\right) R(x,y) = -Q(x) Q(y) \ \ \ (x,y\in J).\] (Observe that the kernel of $[D,(I-K)^{-1}]$ is $(\partial/\partial x + \partial/\partial y ) R(x,y)$.)\ \ Hence \[ \left(\sum_k {\partial\over\partial a_k}\right) R(a_j,a_j) = -q_j^2=-(-1)^j {\partial u\over\partial a_j}\, , \] the last by (\ref{airy_5}).
